claims.text: Under room-temperature uniaxial tensile testing, FeNiCrMn HEA will have tensile strength and ductility comparable to or greater than those of the Co-containing Cantor alloy.
The FeNiCrMn HEA is produced by standard metallurgical processing such as casting or wrought processing.
The as-processed FeNiCrMn HEA has a relatively homogeneous microstructure.
FeNiCrMn samples will be subjected to controlled uniaxial tensile loading with strain tracked by digital image correlation.
Testing will be performed at room temperature, under ambient atmosphere, and at a strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The FeNiCrMn HEA has refined grain boundaries.
A homogeneous microstructure and refined grain boundaries may promote effective dislocation movement and strain hardening.
Removing Co from the alloy could modify phase stability.
Removing Co from the alloy could modify stacking-fault energy.
The proposed changes in phase stability and stacking-fault energy could favorably balance dislocation activity.
Favorably balanced dislocation activity would improve work hardening and ductility during deformation.
FeNiCrMn HEA will demonstrate a high strain-hardening rate and sufficient yield strength.
FeNiCrMn HEA will meet or exceed the ductility and overall mechanical-performance benchmarks of Co-containing Cantor alloys under similar test conditions.
The proposed performance relationship may not hold at elevated temperatures.
Processing conditions that substantially alter the microstructural state may invalidate the proposed performance relationship.
Minor compositional variations, processing history, and microstructural instabilities could affect the measured mechanical properties of FeNiCrMn HEA.
Differences in composition, processing history, and microstructural stability make direct comparison with the Cantor alloy uncertain.
